newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra says no big Losec price change '97.
newsitem.headline: Astra says no big Losec price change '97.

text.p: Swedish pharmaceutical company Astra AB said on Wednesday it did not see any dramatic changes in the price of its blockbuster anti-ulcer agent Losec in 1997.
It also downplayed the negative price effects of parallel imports.
"We don't see any dramatic changes this year in regard to Losec prices," Astra's chief executive Hakan Mogren told a news conference.
"What has a dilution effect price wise is to a certain extent parallel trading. It is, however, important to put this in perspective.
"Parallel trading amounts to two percent of Astra's total sales and four percent of Astra's sales in Europe."
Parallel trading is when retailers, which have bought Losec from Astra, export the drug to countries where retailers must normally pay a higher price.
This puts pressure on other retailers' prices as well as on Astra's price.
Mogren added that the research and development budget for 1997 will be about eight billion crowns.
